sections.h2: Which Oakland County offices handle property tax?
sections.html:
Three layers touch an Oakland County tax bill: the local city, village or township treasurer, the county treasurer, and the county Equalization Division. Current-year bills are collected locally. Once a bill goes unpaid past the winter period, the county treasurer takes over collection.

  • Oakland County Treasurer: delinquent taxes, foreclosure and personal property tax, 1200 North Telegraph Road, Dept 479, Building 12 East, Pontiac, MI 48341, phone 248-858-0611, open 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. on weekdays.
  • Equalization Division: checks assessed values across the county, phone 248-858-0740, open 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. on weekdays.
  • Local treasurer: current summer and winter bills for your city, village or township.
  • Local assessor: the value on your bill and any exemption questions.
  • Business personal property: the treasurer's second line, 248-858-0622.

For the fourteen units the county assesses, Equalization keeps separate lines: 248-858-8793 for property transfers and homestead claims, and 248-858-0776 for appraisal records and tax descriptions. Use them if you sold or bought recently and the bill still shows the earlier owner.

Equalization works across 52 assessing jurisdictions, adjusting each class of property so they all reach a common level of valuation. The division also decides homestead exemption questions, reassesses ownership transfers and reviews millage rollback calculations. For fourteen units, including Novi Township, Lyon Township, South Lyon, Pontiac and Rochester, it acts as the assessor itself and takes all assessment questions.

sections.h2: What does Oakland County look like for a home seller?
sections.html:
Oakland County is a large Metro Detroit county with 867 square miles of land and 1,288,337 residents in the Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate. Pontiac is where the county's tax and records offices sit. Housing is mostly owner-occupied, at 72.7%, and the median owner-occupied home was valued at $343,600 for 2020 to 2024.

Median household income runs $97,760, and median gross rent is $1,376. The county counted 569,537 housing units in 2025 and issued 2,023 building permits that year.

Because the county is so large, ask the local assessor which school and special districts apply to your parcel, since the millage total depends on them.

sections.h2: How are Oakland County taxes calculated and appealed?
sections.html:
A bill equals taxable value divided by 1,000 and multiplied by the millage total for the parcel's taxing units. Assessed value is about half of market value, and taxable value is capped at the lesser of assessed value or the prior year's taxable value times the inflation multiplier, with a 5% ceiling. A change of ownership removes the cap for the following year.

Valuation appeals begin at the local March Board of Review. Michigan law gives owners one chance a year to challenge a residential value there, and the Michigan Tax Tribunal is the next step, with residential petitions due July 31 after a March appearance. File the petition with the board of review for your city or township.

Relief programs sit mostly with the local unit. Cities such as Novi publish a poverty exemption application and a summer tax deferral process, and the county treasurer offers repayment help once a balance is delinquent.

sections.h2: How do you pay Oakland County property tax online?
sections.html:
Oakland County runs a countywide payment portal through PayIt for current bills, delinquent balances and personal property tax. You search by street address or parcel number, then pay as a guest or with an account. The portal lets you pay current taxes on several parcels in the same city, village or township in one visit.

  • Debit and credit cards carry a 3.5% fee.
  • eCheck or ACH payments carry a $2.50 fee.
  • The old $2 statement fee is gone.
  • Cash goes through a barcode from the treasurer's office, accepted at participating retail locations up to $1,000 with a $4.99 convenience fee.
  • Mail and an in-person drop box marked Tax Payments Only are still available for delinquent balances.

Payment history in the portal starts with payments made on or after July 1, 2025. A payment made against the wrong tax year is not transferable, so read the Available Bills list before you check out.

sections.h2: What happens when property taxes go unpaid in Oakland County?
sections.html:
Unpaid Oakland County tax moves to the county treasurer on March 1 and heads toward foreclosure over three years. The county cites MCL 211.78 for this schedule. A 4% administrative fee and interest of 1% per month attach to the original delinquency, and a $15 notification fee comes on October 1.

Oakland County tax foreclosure steps listed by the county treasurer
WhenWhat happens
March 1, year onePrior year's unpaid tax turns delinquent and is payable to the county
March 1, year twoProperty is forfeited to the treasurer, with a $235 minimum fee and 18% yearly interest back to the prior March 1
June 1 to January 31Notification visit, lender notices and newspaper notice fees are added
January or FebruaryAdministrative show cause hearing, then a circuit court foreclosure hearing
March 31Last day to pay everything owed and keep the property
April 1Property is foreclosed
July 1Former owners must file notice of intent to claim any sale proceeds
July to NovemberAuction

For the current cycle, the county's notices state that owners of 2024 and earlier unpaid tax must pay by March 31, 2027. A notice from Title Check LLC may arrive by mail. Respond to it or call the treasurer at 248-858-0611 if you cannot pay in full.

sections.h2: Is there help for Oakland County owners behind on tax?
sections.html:
Yes, the county treasurer arranges payment schedules and refers owners to other programs. The office posts a financial assistance page and a foreclosure prevention page, and contractors visit delinquent parcels to hand over information. Do not wait for the final notice, because fees and the 18% interest on forfeited parcels keep adding up each month.

Former owners can also claim surplus when a foreclosed parcel sells for more than the debt. The county's timeline has claimants file by July 1, learn of any proceeds the following January, file with the court between February and May, and receive payment within 21 days of the court's order.

sections.h2: How do you sell an Oakland County house with tax due?
sections.html:
Order an official delinquent tax statement before you list. Title companies, owners and others can buy one through the county's Property Gateway system, and it shows what the county treasurer holds against the parcel. The local treasurer will give you the current-year balance separately.

At the Register of Deeds, a warranty deed or any deed with a warranty clause needs a tax certification from the county treasurer, which costs $5. That certification confirms taxes are up to date. If back taxes are owed, the title company pays them from the seller's proceeds so the certification can issue and the deed can be recorded. See the county's Register of Deeds guide for recording costs.

faqs.q: Who do I pay in Oakland County if my tax is current?
faqs.a: Pay your city, village or township treasurer. The county treasurer takes payment once a bill has become delinquent, and its portal can handle both kinds in the same system.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to prevent foreclosure on 2024 taxes?
faqs.a: March 31, 2027. The Oakland County Treasurer's notices set that date as the last day to pay unpaid 2024 and earlier taxes and keep the property. Foreclosure takes effect April 1.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to pay Oakland County taxes by card?
faqs.a: The county portal adds 3.5% on debit and credit cards. An eCheck or ACH payment costs $2.50, and the older $2 statement fee has been dropped.

faqs.q: Does the county or my city decide my home's value?
faqs.a: Your city or township assessor sets it, except in fourteen units where the county Equalization Division is the assessor. The county equalizes values among all 52 assessing jurisdictions.

faqs.q: Can a home with delinquent county taxes still be sold?
faqs.a: Yes. The title company pays the county balance at closing, including the 4% fee and interest, and the seller's proceeds cover it. Request a delinquent tax statement first so you know the exact payoff.
